indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B1.4.1.1: Demonstrate understanding of the concept of energy, its various forms and sources and the ways in which it can be transformed and conserved
indicator.objective: Understand energy and give examples of its uses

skills.description: State in simple words that energy is what enables us to do work
Give examples of everyday activities that use energy
Name simple sources of energy for everyday activities
Explain simply what happens when there is no energy

misconceptions: Only people need energy; animals and machines do not.
Food is not energy; it is just something we eat.
Energy is something you can always see.

questions.stem: What gives you the power to walk and run?
questions.explanation: Energy is what gives you the power to do things like walk and run.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think objects like chairs give them energy.

questions.stem: Which of these activities uses energy?
hints: You use your legs to push off the ground.
questions.explanation: Jumping uses energy because it requires your body to move and work.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think sitting quietly uses no energy at all.

questions.stem: Where do people get the energy to work and play?
questions.explanation: People get energy from the food they eat.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think they get energy from just resting.

questions.stem: What happens to a car when it runs out of fuel?
questions.explanation: A car stops moving when it runs out of fuel because it has no energy.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a car can move without fuel.

questions.stem: Which of these uses energy from electricity?
questions.explanation: A fan uses electrical energy to spin and give breeze.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all objects use electricity.

questions.stem: Energy is best described as...
options: What enables us to do work
hints: Think about what you need to run.
questions.explanation: Energy is what enables us to do work, move, and play.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think energy is always visible.

questions.stem: What is the main source of energy for plants to make their food?
hints: It is in the sky during the day.
questions.explanation: The sun is the main source of energy for plants to make food.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think plants only get energy from the soil.

questions.stem: Kofi is pushing a heavy box. What is he using?
hints: His body needs energy to push.
questions.explanation: Kofi is using energy to push the heavy box.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not associate physical work with energy.

questions.stem: Ama has not eaten all day. How will she feel?
hints: Without food, you have no energy.
questions.explanation: Ama will feel weak because she has no energy from food.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think skipping meals makes you stronger.

questions.stem: Which of these activities does NOT need much energy?
questions.explanation: Sleeping in bed requires much less energy than running or playing.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think sleeping uses no energy at all, but the body still needs some.

questions.stem: Name one thing that gives you energy.
questions.explanation: Food is the main source of energy for people.
questions.misconception: Pupils may name things that do not provide energy, like a pencil.

questions.stem: What do we call the thing that helps us do work?
questions.explanation: Energy is what helps us do work.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse energy with a physical object.

questions.stem: Why does a person need to eat food before playing football?
questions.explanation: Food provides the energy needed to run and play football.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think eating before playing makes you tired.

questions.stem: What happens to a torch when its battery runs out?
hints: The battery gives the torch energy.
questions.explanation: A torch stops giving light when its battery is dead because it has no energy.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a torch can work without a battery.

questions.stem: Which of these is a source of energy for a moving car?
hints: The car goes to the petrol station.
questions.explanation: Petrol (fuel) is the source of energy for a car to move.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think cars run on water.

questions.stem: Which of these shows the use of energy in the home?
options: A book lying on a table
hints: Energy is needed to change the food.
questions.explanation: Cooking food on a stove uses energy (heat energy).
questions.misconception: Pupils may not realize cooking uses energy.

questions.stem: Explain what happens to a person who has not eaten for a long time.

criteria.description: States the person will feel weak or tired
Explains that the person has no energy from food

questions.explanation: A person who has not eaten for a long time will feel weak because they have no energy from food.

questions.stem: Why do we say energy is needed to do work?
options: Because energy gives us the strength to move and act
hints: Think about pushing a heavy object.
What gives you the power to push it?
questions.explanation: Energy gives us the strength and power to move and do work.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think work requires no energy.

questions.stem: Tell me two activities you did today that used energy.
questions.explanation: Walking, playing, and writing are all activities that use energy.

questions.stem: Which statement is TRUE about energy?
options: Energy is only found in food
Energy can never be used up
Living things and machines need energy to work
questions.explanation: Both living things and machines need energy to work.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think only humans use energy.
